RESOLUTION OF TATTNALL COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS TO REPEAL AND RESCIND AN ORDINANCE TO TEMPORARILY LIMIT OLTDOOR BURNING DUE TO DROUGHT CONDITIONS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES ALLOWED BY LAW.

WHEREAS, on or about April 6, 2026, the Governing Authority of Tattnall County, Georgia (the “County”), as empowered by law, adopted AN ORDINANCE TO TEMPORARILY LIMIT OUTDOOR BURNING DUE TO DROUGHT CONDITIONS (“Ordinance”), wherein the County restricted all open burning of yard debris, including leaves, limbs, grass, and other vegetative matter in the unincorporated area of Tattnall County and wherein the County provided that no person shall ignite or allow the burning of yard debris outdoors except as provided in the Ordinance;

WHEREAS, the Ordinance was adopted in cooperation with and in response to an Executive Order from the Governor of the State of Georgia, who declared that severe drought conditions existed at the time of the Ordinance and that such conditions significantly increased the risk of wildfires and the spread of uncontrolled fires statewide; and

WHEREAS, on or about May 5, 2026, by Executive Order, the Governor lifted the statewide burn ban except as to seventeen counties (“affected counties”), excluding Tattnall County, and the Governor also lifted the administrative order from the Georgia Forestry Commission instituting a temporary burn ban, except as to the affected counties (See a copy of Executive Order dated May 5, 2026 attached hereto as Exhibit A).

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Governing Authority in public meeting assembled, and it is hereby resolved by the authority of the same, that:

- 1. The Ordinance referenced above is hereby repealed and rescinded; provided that, any person or entity that desires to engage in the ignition and/or open burning of yard debris, including leaves, limbs, grass, and other vegetative matter in the unincorporated area of Tattnall County, shall continue to exercise due care in doing'so and shall follow all laws, rules and regulations of the State of Georgia that apply to such activities, as well as all other ordinances, rules and regulations of the County applicable to such activities.

- 2. This Resolution shall take effect immediately upon its adoption and the County Clerk or other official or agent of the County shall place public record of this Resolution in the minutes of the County.

On April 22, 2026, I issued Executive Order No. 04.22.26.01, declaring a State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires in 91 counties in South Georgia that were at high risk for wildfires; and

The State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires adopted and incorporated an administrative order from the Georgia Forestry Commission implementing a temporary burn ban in the 91 counties covered by the declaration; and —

Although the risk of wildfires remains high, favorable weather conditions have lowered the risk in many areas, and in consultation with the Georgia Forestry Commission and the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency, I have determined that the State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires can be lifted in many of the affected counties.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTIONS 38-3-28 AND 38-3-51, AND THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That the State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires shall be lifted in all counties except for: Appling, Atkinson, Bacon, Berrien, Brantley, Camden, Charlton, Clinch, Coffee, Echols, Glynn, Jeff Davis, Lanier, Lowndes, Pierce, Ware, and Wayne counties (the “Affected Counties”).
9: That the administrative order from the Georgia Forestry Commission instituting a temporary burn ban, which was incorporated into. Executive Order No. 04.22.26.01 as if issued therein, is correspondingly lifted in all counties except for the Affected Counties as described in this Order.
10:
ORDERED: That except as modified by this Order, the provisions of Executive Order No. 04.22.26.01 shall remain in effect until the State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires expires or the provisions are otherwise terminated via subsequent Executive Order.
